title.narrative: Amendment no 1 - NDICI CHALLENGE/2023/442-297 - Promoting and measuring universal and meaningful digital connectivity

description.narrative: Contract related to: Amendment no 1 - NDICI CHALLENGE/2023/442-297 - Promoting and measuring universal and meaningful digital connectivity - The action intends to promote the EU¿s vision of digitalisation in the multilateral system, and in multi-stakeholder and multilateral fora. Advancing the EU¿s participation and role in a specific range of topics will on the one hand promote the EU¿s vision and on the other hand reduce the risk of propagation of non-democratic and non-human centric developments in the digital domain.¿With the objective of promoting Open Internet Governance and responsible use of Artificial Intelligence (AI), the action aims to enhance participation and cooperation of Civil Society in multilateral and multistakeholder fora with regards to digital for development, internet governance and digital rights and inclusion; as well as to promote an EU human-centric approach to AI. Furthermore, this action will contribute to the promotion of the implementation of the UN Secretary-General Roadmap for Digital Cooperation and the Global Digital Compact. In the context of promoting regulatory convergence, digital sovereignty and digital citizenship, this action will foster the harmonization of digital policies and the cybersecurity global normative framework, strengthen capacity building and support tools for global monitoring of digital transformation indicators. It will contribute to the creation and maintenance of digital accessible eGovernance ecosystems and networks of Open-Source Software developers, the promotion of `digital rights and principles¿ and CSO participation in policy debate.  This action is designed such that future components of the Multilateralism and Digital programme can be adequately integrated.The Action aims will be implemented through direct management and indirect management

Quarterly peer learning platform sessions of tech companies held in Q3 and Q4 2023 and throughout 2024

Quarterly peer learning platform sessions of tech companies held in Q3 and Q4 2023 and throughout 2024.These were held throughout 2023 with none in 2024 and none planned for the remainder of the year.Quarterly peer learning platform sessions of tech companies held in Q3 and Q4 2023 and throughout 2024.These were held throughout 2023 with none in 2024 and none planned for the remainder of the year.Quarterly peer learning platform sessions of tech companies held in Q3 and Q4 2023 and throughout 2024.These were held throughout 2023 with none in 2024 and none planned for the remainder of the year.In calendar year 2023 BTech organised and carried out a series of six sessions out of which two fall within the scope of the project webinars introducing selfdefined tech companies and their representatives to topics covered in the four BTech focus areas as related to the UNGPs as well as crosscutting workstreams undertaken by BTech. This Peer Learning Platform offered an opportunity for tech companies with nascent human rights functions to explore the UNGPs both through instructive modules led by BTech experts and in case studies or examples presented by practitioners. The titles and dates of the six sessions as well as summary notes from each session and the original slide decks are as followsPLP Session 5 Accountability and Remedy 13 September 2023 Summary note and slide deckPLP Session 6 Stakeholder Engagement and the Technology Sector 8 November 2023 Summary note and slide deckBetween 520 participants joined the sessions representing 515 companies each. The BTech team held each session twice save for 4 due to summer holidays once in a EuropeanAsiafriendly time slot and a second in a time slot more convenient for the Americas so as to facilitate participation across geographies in the hopes of attracting registrants from beyond B Techs existing network. In addition to participants from companies working in the digital tech sector the PLP series attracted interest from several civil society organisations as well as tech companies engaged in hardwaresupply chain work. Although BTech since its inception has focused predominantly on the human rights impacts of digital tech products and services in end use the registration of these external prospective participants suggests that there is scope to expand the constituency of BTech activity and consultations. After this initial trial of the peerlearning format based on company feedback we transformed the format into dropins and made the introductory material available online. We are currently in conversations with UN Global Compact New York to integrate the materials into their learning platform.

title.narrative: Establish consistent, human rightsbased approaches for United Nations entities in their development and use of digital technologies, setting a global example for States and companies.

description.narrative: Thanks to the EU support provided through this project, OHCHR achieved the significant milestone of the adoption of the Guidance of the SecretaryGeneral on Human Rights Due Diligence for Digital Technology Use by the Executive Committee in May 2024 and included as normative guidance in the UN systemwide AI governance policy framework endorsed by the UN System Chief Executives Board. OHCHR has driven the rollout across the UNsystem and, in the short time period, the HRDD Guidance has already been applied (see case studies) by UNHCR, and ILO amongst others. The HRDD Guidance has also sparked interest beyond its initial targets of UN agencies, with institutions such as the World Bank, EU Delegations and various States expressing appreciation for its usefulness, and applicability to public authorities use of technology beyond the UN system.
